name: comqtt-live-listener-set-reconciliation
instr:
Allow a running CoMQTT broker to reconcile its complete listener set without interrupting endpoints that remain valid. A request should produce a deterministic generation result while transport changes, client retirement, configuration loading, and management access behave as one operation. Existing startup and protocol behavior must remain unchanged when live reconciliation is unused.

Reconciliation is atomic: the previous generation remains wholly visible and serving until every desired endpoint is prepared, and any rejection rolls back prepared resources without disconnecting clients or changing ownership. A successful commit classifies every identifier as unchanged, added, replaced, or removed, reports rejections when unsuccessful, retains clients on unchanged listeners, and afterward drains clients from replaced or removed listeners. Equivalent definitions compare by meaningful transport settings across TCP, Net, Unix, QUIC, WebSocket, HTTP, and health listeners, while address, TLS, or zero-RTT changes cause replacement. TCP acceptance starts only after commit, Unix pathname ownership survives rollback and transfers safely, and QUIC retains its configured TLS, zero-RTT, and stream-generation behavior. Externally supplied Net listeners can remain or be removed, but reconstruction is rejected without surrendering the active listener. WebSocket listeners preserve MQTT framing, whereas HTTP management and health listeners retain HTTP semantics and never establish MQTT clien
